info.name: Food Delivery - Payment Flow Demo
info.description:
Demonstrates the Order -> RabbitMQ -> Payment -> RabbitMQ -> Order asynchronous flow.

Prerequisites: RabbitMQ container running, MongoDB Atlas reachable, and service-registry, api-gateway, order-service, payment-service all UP on http://localhost:8761.

Run the requests top to bottom. Steps 2-4 read back state that was changed entirely by RabbitMQ messages - no Postman call touches Payment Service directly.

variable.description: API Gateway - the single entry point. Swap to http://localhost:9013 (order) or http://localhost:9004 (payment) only if the gateway is down.
Captured automatically by step 1's test script.

request.description:
Manual initiation endpoint, used here to prove idempotency: the order is already paid, so PaymentService returns the existing record instead of creating a second charge. Watch the console for 'is already paid ... skipping'.

This is NOT the customer checkout path - the customer never calls Payment Service.

item.name: 6. Failure path - order above gateway limit

exec: console.log('Now re-run steps 2 and 3. Expect payment FAILED and order PAYMENT_FAILED.');
console.log('No config change needed: 999999 is already above the default limit of 100000.');

request.description:
999999 exceeds the default payment.gateway.max-amount of 100000, so the simulated gateway declines it.

After running this, re-run step 2 (payment status FAILED with a failureReason) and step 3 (order status PAYMENT_FAILED). This proves the failure branch travels back over RabbitMQ too, not just the happy path.
